Lifespan shutdown sets the stopping event and awaits the scheduler task. The whole reconciliation operation spans Docker SDK calls, journal/database/filesystem operations, and per-generation processing. Resolves `engine.target` in a worker, acquires a socket slot, constructs the connection, enters `direct_connect`, accepts the client, and awaits `pump`. Failures can originate in the worker-side engine, WebSocket connection/context manager, ASGI client operations, or relay callbacks—not one closed transport exception family.

After cancelling and gathering any pending read, calls `await iterator.aclose()`. Catches `Exception` and `CancelledError`, records only the exception class, and completes shielded/drained cleanup rather than replacing the stream outcome. `aclose()` can execute arbitrary async-generator `finally` code or custom iterator teardown; the iterator protocol does not constrain its exception types.

Calls `await resource.aclose()` separately for response and client. Each failure is reduced to a type-only log, allowing the other resource to close. `UpstreamLease.close()` owns one shared cleanup task and drains it despite caller cancellation. Response/client close may execute SDK/transport cleanup with implementation-dependent exceptions; narrowing would allow the first close failure to prevent the second resource’s release or replace the delivery outcome.

Calls `task.result()` for completed inbound/outbound/watch tasks. Known limits map to 1009, HTTP authorization failures to 1008, transport disconnects are accepted, and other exceptions map to **1011**. The consuming `pump` passes this result to `_shutdown`, which cancels tasks, closes the client, and gathers all tasks. Tasks include ASGI reads/writes, upstream WebSocket operations, and a supplied identity guard; an unexpected callback/task exception still needs bounded shutdown and a fixed public close code.
